conventions.axes: Y-up, right-handed; camera looks down -Z by default; ground is the XZ plane at y = 0

style.name: Tiny Planet
style.description: A whole world on one small rotating globe that fills the frame: a faceted low-poly sphere on a warm cream backdrop, lit by a fixed sun so the right limb is always a blue night crescent. A bare grey gridded ball turns under a fixed camera; streams of small word chips rain onto it, and from every landing point a front spreads along the surface: land rises out of the ball, colours in (sea, sand, grass, rock, snow), then trees, houses, roads and clouds pop up, and warm lamps come on as they turn into the night side. One planner (globe.js) places everything in latitude/longitude, computes when each front reaches each vertex and feature in closed form, and writes the score.
motion: The camera is locked; the globe turns about its axis (spin keys in degrees). One fast half-turn is the reveal.
Word chips fall in streams from outside the frame and shrink into the ground where they land.
From each landing point a front spreads along the surface (outQuad): vertices rise with an outBack overshoot, facets colour in behind a pale leading edge.
Trees, houses and clouds pop (outBack) when a later 'life' front reaches them; roads draw outward from the town centre.
Lamps are additive points whose level is the night factor of their current world normal: they come on as they turn into the crescent.

beats.label: It only knows what it read

notes.mechanism: globe.js: everything is [lat, lon] on the globe. Word-chip streams land at a place; a front spreads from each landing (outQuad) and the closed-form arrival time at each vertex / facet / tree / house / road sample drives rise, colour and pop. Reads reach only their own cap, so the far side stays bare until the last beat.
